title: The Courtyard House
summary: A family home arranged around a shaded central court, where timber, dark brick and deep overhangs temper the Rajasthani sun.
concept: The house turns inward. Living spaces wrap a planted courtyard that pulls light and breeze into every room, while a heavy, dark-clad outer shell keeps heat and street noise at bay. At dusk the timber-lined interiors glow through full-height glazing, reversing the building's daytime reserve.
description:
Designed for a multi-generational family, the plan separates a quiet private wing from a generous social core. A single long verandah ties kitchen, dining and living to the garden, with sliding screens that open the ground floor almost entirely in winter.

Passive strategies — stack ventilation through the stair, shaded glazing and a high-mass envelope — keep the house comfortable with minimal mechanical cooling.
specs: Structure: RCC frame with load-bearing brick

title: White Ledge Villa
summary: A lakeside retreat of stacked white volumes and cantilevered terraces, opening onto an infinity pool and the hills beyond.
concept: Three white ledges step down the slope, each framing a different view of the lake. The pool extends the lowest ledge into the landscape, so water, terrace and horizon read as one continuous plane.
description:
Built as a weekend home for hosting, the villa organises guest suites on the upper ledge and an open entertaining level at the water's edge. Deep timber soffits shade the glazing and warm the otherwise mineral palette.

A sculptural stair connects all levels, doubling as a gallery for the client's collection.

title: Meridian Workplace
summary: A headquarters fit-out built around daylight — glass-walled studios, a concrete-and-timber spine and calm, flexible work zones.
concept: A single circulation spine runs the length of the floor plate, with focus rooms, collaboration areas and a cafe arranged along it like rooms on a street. Glass partitions keep daylight moving deep into the plan.
description:
The brief asked for a workplace that could absorb 40% growth without rebuilding. A modular grid of furniture, power and lighting lets teams reconfigure in an afternoon.

Exposed concrete soffits, oak and black steel keep the palette restrained and durable.

title: Atrium Tower
summary: A faceted glass office tower whose folded crown and full-height atrium bring daylight into the heart of the building.
concept: The tower's form is cut back at the crown and base, creating a sheltered public forecourt and a sculpted skyline profile. A twelve-storey atrium acts as the building's lung and social heart.
description:
High-performance double glazing and vertical fins reduce solar gain on the west façade, while the atrium drives stack ventilation in shoulder seasons.

The ground floor is given back to the street with a cafe, lobby gallery and landscaped plaza.

title: Ivory Apartment
summary: A soft, tonal apartment interior in ivory, oat and travertine — calm rooms with curved forms and diffused light.
concept: One colour, many textures. Walls, joinery and upholstery share a single ivory tone so that light, shadow and material grain become the decoration.
description:
The existing plan was opened to connect living, dining and a reading corner. Curved joinery softens corners and hides storage, and a layered lighting scheme moves from bright morning to warm evening.

Furniture is a mix of bespoke pieces and work by Indian makers.

title: Timber Ridge Residence
summary: A hillside home of timber and dark steel that follows the slope, with a double-height living room facing the valley.
concept: Rather than flatten the site, the house steps with it. A long timber volume floats over a dark base, opening at its end to a double-height room framed on the view.
description: Local deodar-tone timber, stone retaining walls and a standing-seam roof suit the hill climate. Large overhangs protect glazing from monsoon rain while admitting low winter sun.

title: Garden Kothi Renewal
summary: A 1970s bungalow reworked for a new generation — opened up, re-lit and reconnected to its garden.
concept: Keep the bones, change the light. The original brick shell and terrazzo floors were retained, while new openings and a lightwell transformed the dark centre of the house.
description: Partitions were removed to form a continuous living and kitchen space, the roof was insulated and the services entirely renewed. A warm, crafted interior honours the house's mid-century roots.

title: Pavilion Garden
summary: A glass garden pavilion, reflecting pool and coastal planting that turn a weekend estate into a single landscape.
concept: The landscape is the architecture. A slim steel-and-glass pavilion sits lightly at the end of a long reflecting pool, aligned with the sunset.
description: Native, salt-tolerant planting and permeable paving manage monsoon run-off, while shaded outdoor rooms extend living into the garden year-round.

title: Noir House
summary: A compact black-clad urban house with slot windows, a private courtyard and calm, light-filled interiors.
concept: Closed to the street, open to the sky. A dark, finely ribbed façade gives privacy on a busy road, while the interiors open to a planted courtyard and rooftop garden.
description: Currently in design development, the project explores a dark exterior palette that reduces visual mass at night and a bright, minimal interior that maximises daylight.
